newsitem.title: CROATIA: Hotelier Laguna sees 4-5 mln kuna net for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Hotelier Laguna sees 4-5 mln kuna net for 1996.

text.p: Croatian seaside hotelier Plava Laguna said on Wednesday it expected between four and five million kuna net profit for 1996 thanks to a better season.
As profit rumours reached the market, Laguna's shares rose to 1,500 kuna on Zagreb's bourse this week from 1,060 earlier this month.

"Our total income was 190 million kuna, which is good for the kind of season we had," finance director Marko Simonetti told Reuters by telephone. "June and July were bad but we did much better in August."
Simonetti put 1996 overnights at 1.244 million, up from an expected 1-1.1 milion and only 712,000 in 1995, when Laguna's loss totalled 28.6 million kuna.
That was before an international peace agreement was struck to end the war in former Yugoslavia while tourists, foreigners in particular, were wary of visiting the region.
Although trade picked up last year, the company still suffered the burden of huge costs, Simonetti said, adding that strong kuna also hampered the country's key strategic branch.
Laguna is one of the largest tourist companies with over 24,000 beds in various hotel and camping facilities in and around the scenic town of Porec on the Istrian peninsula.
"These problems are well known, but they are a general Croatian issue. The kuna is too strong, on the other hand our inputs are very high," Simonetti complained.
But he said Laguna looked forward to an even better summer this year producing a 30-percent increase in overnights.

"This may not be reflected in profits because of difficult conditions. We also plan extensive investments in maintenance and upgrading the facilities," Simonetti said, but declined to reveal precise investment plans.
He also would not venture a profit forecast for 1997 so early on.

Troubled Croatian bank Privredna Banka gained control of Laguna after swapping shares with the state privatisation agency. Banque Indosuez also has a 12.5-percent stake and private shareholders around 39 percent in Laguna. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
